chunk_findings.detail:
In `glob_clashes`, when one live lease overlaps the current item on more than one glob, the loop still appends only `pairs[0]` for that item:
```python
pairs = conflicts(globs, lease.globs, shared)
if pairs:
    out.append(Clash(other_id, pairs[0], lease))
```
So for current globs `["brief.py", "lane_views.py"]` held by another lease, `glob_clashes` returns one `Clash`, not two, even though both globs conflict. Any refusal report built from this list will still omit `lane_views.py`; the original "one overlap per refusal" bug persists when a single holder holds multiple requested files.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/admission.py:glob_clashes

chunk_findings.detail:
Both queued-behind refusals now print `ahead.globs`, but `ahead` is the queued lease ahead of the refused item, so `.globs` is the whole set of globs the ahead item asked for, not the globs of the refused item that are queued behind it. Input: the refused item asks for `brief.py`; the ahead lease holds `brief.py`, `lane_views.py`, and `reporting.py`. The new message says:
`those files (brief.py, lane_views.py, reporting.py) are queued behind ...`
even though only `brief.py` is the refused item's conflicting file. The message should list the refused item's conflicting globs (or the intersection with its current request), not the full `ahead.globs`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/reservations.py:201, ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim_guard_queued.py:25

chunk_findings.detail: `clash_report` returns `[oid for oid, _lz, _p in clashes]` without deduplicating item IDs. `glob_clashes` represents one entry per overlapping `(mine, theirs)` pair, so a single conflicting lease holding two globs overlapped by the claim yields two entries for the same item, e.g. `("B", lease_B, ("src/a.py","src/a.py"))` and `("B", lease_B, ("src/b.py","src/b.py"))` produce `_ids == ["B", "B"]`. The docstring says this is the list of "every conflicting item id ... a waiter must wait on each"; any caller that uses it to append `lease.waiting` entries will enqueue the same item twice. The added test only covers two distinct item IDs, so it does not catch this.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/common.py:clash_report

chunk_findings.detail: The test only checks that both glob strings and both holder strings appear in `main`; it never checks that each holder is attached to the correct glob. A wrong implementation that emitted `src/a.py ... held by agent-holder2` and `src/b.py ... held by HOLDER` would still pass. Since the promise being fixed is specifically to list every conflicting glob *with its holder*, the association is the core behavior and should be asserted.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_wait_claim_agree.py:test_claim_refusal_lists_every_conflicting_holder

chunk_findings.detail: `glob_clashes` still keeps only `pairs[0]` per other item (`out.append(Clash(other_id, pairs[0], lease))` and the offered-path twin). A clash record has one pair and no claim-glob list, and `clash_report` is only given those clashes, so the dropped pairs cannot be rebuilt. Input: one live lease held by `sw-cedefaults` on `brief.py`, `lane_views.py`, and `reporting.py`, claim globs that overlap all three. `conflicts()` returns three pairs; the refusal built from this list still names a single glob, which is the failure this change says it fixes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/admission.py:glob_clashes

chunk_findings.detail: `clash_report` always renders `held by {lz.holder}` and has no queue-place branch. Given a clash whose lease is only queued — the case the bug cites for `update --globs` (`those globs are queued behind sw-cedefaults`) — the text is `'src/a.py' overlaps 'src/**' held by sw-cedefaults on Y`, which claims a hold that does not exist and never states queue place.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/common.py:clash_report

chunk_findings.detail: The regression only claims two live holders and checks that both paths and both agent ids appear as substrings before `Recorded:`. It never runs `update --globs` against a queued lease, and a refusal that merely echoes Y's own glob list plus both agent names (without pairing each glob to its holder or queue place) satisfies the asserts, so the stated bug can remain and the test still passes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_wait_claim_agree.py:test_claim_refusal_lists_every_conflicting_holder
